record.context_brief: unresolved disjunction involving local rank and spectrum
record.original_question: Which of the following two assertions is true: first, there exists a measure-preserving automorphism with absolutely continuous spectrum of finite multiplicity; second, every mixing automorphism of positive local rank has mixing of all orders? Here positive local rank means that there exists beta > 0 and a sequence of Rokhlin-tower unions U_j with mu(U_j) -> beta such that, on U_j, every measurable set is asymptotically approximated by unions of tower levels.

evidence.quote: Локальный ранг автоморфизма. Говорят, что автоморфизм T обладает локальным рангом β > 0, если для некоторой последовательности множеств вида U_j = ⋃_{k∈Q_j} T^z B_j, Q_j = {0, 1, . . . , h_j}, выполнены условия: µ(U_j) → β, и для каждого A ∈ B пересечение U_j ∩ A аппроксимируется объединениями некоторого набора этажей в башне.
Одно из утверждений верно, хотя не знаем, какое именно.

Теорема 1.1. Верно по крайней мере одно из следующих утверждений: – существует автоморфизм с конечнократным абсолютно непрерывным спектром; – всякий перемешивающий автоморфизм положительного локального ранга обладает кратным перемешиванием.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic Lebesgue probability space and let $T:X\to X$ be an invertible measure-preserving automorphism. Recall the following definitions.

(a) $T$ has *absolutely continuous spectrum of finite multiplicity* if the maximal spectral type of the Koopman operator $U_T f = f\circ T$ acting on $L^2_0(X,\mu)$ (the orthogonal complement of constants) is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on the circle, and the spectral multiplicity function is bounded.

(b) $T$ is *mixing* if $\mu(T^{-n}A\cap B)\to\mu(A)\mu(B)$ for all $A,B\in\mathcal{B}$ as $|n|\to\infty$. It has *mixing of all orders* (multiple mixing) if for every $k\ge 2$ and all $A_0,\dots,A_k\in\mathcal{B}$,
$$\mu(A_0\cap T^{-n_1}A_1\cap\cdots\cap T^{-n_k}A_k)\to\prod_{i=0}^{k}\mu(A_i)$$
whenever $n_1, n_2-n_1, \dots, n_k-n_{k-1}\to\infty$.

(c) $T$ has *positive local rank* if there exists $\beta>0$ and a sequence of Rokhlin towers with bases $B_j$ and heights $h_j+1$, giving sets $U_j=\bigsqcup_{k=0}^{h_j} T^k B_j$, such that $\mu(U_j)\to\beta$ and for every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ the intersection $U_j\cap A$ is asymptotically approximated (in measure) by unions of levels $T^k B_j$ of the $j$-th tower.

Prove that at least one of the following two statements holds:
(i) there exists a measure-preserving automorphism with absolutely continuous spectrum of finite multiplicity;
(ii) every mixing automorphism of positive local rank has mixing of all orders.

Determine which of the two statements is true.
artifact.category_tag: Ergodic theory: spectrum and multiple mixing
artifact.status_search_result: The disjunction is established (at least one of the two assertions holds), but neither alternative is known to be true individually. Both Banach's problem on existence of an automorphism with finite-multiplicity absolutely continuous spectrum and Rokhlin's problem on multiple mixing for mixing automorphisms of positive local rank remain open in the recent ergodic-theory literature.

status_evidence.title: Multiple mixing, 75 years of Rokhlin's problem
status_evidence.snippet: Survey by Ryzhikov discussing the still-open Rokhlin multiple mixing problem and related local-rank classes.
status_evidence.claim: Rokhlin's problem on multiple mixing remains open, including for positive local rank classes.

status_evidence.title: Spectral theory of dynamical systems (Kanigowski–Lemańczyk survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey notes that the existence of a measure-preserving transformation with finite multiplicity absolutely continuous spectrum (Banach's problem) is open.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of an automorphism with absolutely continuous spectrum of finite multiplicity is an open problem.
